_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Bangalore's urban water supply. UNLIKE Chennai's supply-overview (anchored on the ADB CCRWSSP IEE March 2026) and Madurai's (anchored on the ADB TNUFIP Tranche 2 IEEs), Bangalore does NOT have a publicly available ADB IEE we can extract engineering numbers from. The single highest-leverage primary document is the WELL Labs Bengaluru Urban Water Balance report (Jan 2024), which is behind a registration gate. Numbers below are compiled from BWSSB Wikipedia, public BWSSB statements quoted in The Ken (May 2026), IISc Groundwater Outlook of Bengaluru City (April 2025), and the bangalore_data_sources_research audit memo. Fields tagged with _provenance='estimate' or 'reported_no_primary' need verification against the WELL Labs PDF + an ADB Karnataka IEE before being quoted to journalists.

_view_overrides.subtitle: Compiled from BWSSB public statements, IISc Groundwater Outlook (April 2025) and the WELL Labs Bengaluru Urban Water Balance. Engineering numbers from a primary ADB/JICA IEE document remain a follow-up data acquisition - several fields below are best public estimates pending that source.
_view_overrides.demand_caption: Unlike Chennai (impounded reservoirs) and Madurai (gravity feed from Mullaperiyar), Bangalore is fundamentally a pumped city. ~1,450 MLD is lifted ~95 km uphill from the Cauvery against a city demand of ~2,100 MLD - the remaining ~650+ MLD comes from groundwater, illegal extraction, and a tanker market BWSSB itself only partly serves.

_data_provenance_caveats: BWSSB official supply numbers and the WELL Labs bottom-up estimate diverge sharply (e.g. BWSSB cites 800 MLD groundwater extraction; WELL Labs estimates 1,392 MLD). Both are documented below.
Stage V (T.K. Halli, commissioned 16 October 2024) design is 775 MLD but actual delivery is reported at ~400 MLD as of Feb 2026 - the 'expansion only half-delivering' story.
Transmission distance from Cauvery (T.K. Halli intake) to Bangalore is variously cited as 95 km, 98 km, and 100 km depending on the source. We use ~95-100 km as a range.
Population served varies by boundary: BBMP ~10M, GBA 369 wards ~13.5M (post-Nov 2025 delimitation), Bengaluru Urban district ~12.5M.
Wikipedia's 900 MLD supply number is pre-Stage V (Stage IV completion era) - superseded by the post-Stage V ~1,300-1,450 MLD range.

supply_chain: Cauvery River (Krishnaraja Sagar / KRS reservoir + Hemavathi + Harangi + Kabini upstream storage)
T.K. Halli intake on the Cauvery (~95-100 km south of Bangalore)
5-stage Cauvery Water Supply Scheme (Stages I-V, 1974-2024) - pumping water uphill against ~500 m elevation
Cauvery WTPs at T.K. Halli + Tataguni + intermediate stations
Transmission mains delivering up to ~1,450 MLD design (~1,300 MLD actual)
Local resources (largely defunct for potable): TG Halli/Chamaraja Sagar 1933, Hesaraghatta 1894, Arkavathi
Groundwater: BWSSB-managed wells + ~400,000+ private borewells across BBMP/GBA
Tanker market (informal): Kaveriwheels app official tankers + a large private tanker mafia
Distribution: BWSSB ~10.5 lakh service connections (BBMP area), GBA-wide coverage incomplete

WELL Labs Jan 2024 bottom-up urban water balance. 592 MLD HIGHER than BWSSB's official number. The divergence IS the story - presented alongside BWSSB's 800 MLD, not instead of it.

current_supply_mix_mld.supplies: All Bengaluru, peaks in summer crisis
current_supply_mix_mld.note: OpenCity Bengaluru Tanker Water Survey 2024+2025 quantifies tanker dependence but no consolidated MLD published. The Ken (May 2026): Kaveriwheels official tankers ~19K downloads in 14M city; rates Rs 700/5kL official vs Rs 2,850/12kL informal at crisis peak.

_supply_total_note: 1,710 MLD = Cauvery Stages I-V active delivery (~1,310 MLD, taking Stage V at actual ~400 not design ~775) + BWSSB official groundwater (800 MLD). NOT the same as the city's drinking-water-equivalent consumption. Excludes private borewell extraction beyond BWSSB's accounting (WELL Labs would put total resource utilisation at ~2,300+ MLD against this 1,710 MLD).

wtps_summary._note: BWSSB does NOT publish a clean WTP-by-WTP capacity table on its English info pages. Numbers below are compiled from public references and need verification against the WELL Labs report or an ADB Karnataka IEE.
wtps_summary._stage_v_caveat: Stage V actual delivery is ~50% of design as of Feb 2026 due to distribution main + last-mile connection delays in the 110 newly-added villages.
wtps_summary.tk_halli_treatment_complex: Multi-stage WTP complex at T.K. Halli (~95-100 km south of Bangalore), serves as the headworks for all 5 Cauvery stages.

tg_halli_reuse_project.scheme: STP-treated wastewater + Indirect Potable Reuse (IPR), blended in TG Halli reservoir
tg_halli_reuse_project.note: Country's largest indirect-potable-reuse experiment. Repurposes TG Halli/Chamaraja Sagar (1933) which has been defunct for potable supply since the 1990s due to upstream sewage contamination.

distribution._note: Distribution figures here are best public estimates. BWSSB does not publish a consolidated network statistics page. The 11 lakh connections figure is widely cited but the date varies. Per-capita LPCD official vs actual is sharply contested.
distribution.service_area_description: BBMP 198-ward area historically; expanding to GBA 369-ward area post-Nov 2025 delimitation. Many newly-added wards still have partial or zero piped coverage.
distribution._service_connections_note: Widely cited as '~11 lakh connections'. Roughly 70% domestic, 30% non-domestic / commercial. Coverage by ward in the newly-merged 110 villages and GBA peripheral wards is incomplete.
distribution._lpcd_note: BWSSB design standard 150 LPCD for the served population. Many wards receive less than 100 LPCD in practice due to NRW (~40% non-revenue water cited in industry literature) + intermittent supply. Stress wards skew sharply lower; tanker-dependent areas pay multiples for less.

demand._note: Demand figures here are public estimates pending verification against an ADB Karnataka water IEE or WELL Labs published demand projections. Population numbers depend on which boundary is used.
demand._current_demand_caveat: Often cited as 2,000-2,200 MLD across BBMP+GBA. Bangalore lives with a roughly 600-800 MLD shortfall against current demand, plugged by groundwater + tanker market + intermittent rationing.
demand._city_area_gba_note: GBA area encompasses BBMP's 741 sqkm + the newly-added city corporation areas. Total post-Nov 2025 delimitation TBD; we estimate ~1,300+ sqkm pending an authoritative GBA area declaration.

allocation_context._note: Bangalore's water comes from the Cauvery basin, governed by the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) 2007 award + Supreme Court 2018 modification. Karnataka's allocation is shared between irrigation (largest), Bangalore drinking, other urban centres, and rural drinking.
allocation_context._drinking_tmc_note: Karnataka's 14.75 TMC drinking-water share covers Bangalore + Mysuru + other Cauvery-basin urban centres. Bangalore alone is widely cited as needing ~19-24 TMC at current demand.
allocation_context.krs_reservoir_role: Headworks for the Cauvery delivery to Bangalore via T.K. Halli intake. KRS storage + Hemavathi + Harangi + Kabini upstream combined determine Bangalore's annual supply security.
allocation_context._groundwater_dependency_note: BWSSB official: ~800 MLD GW / ~2,300 MLD total = ~35%. WELL Labs bottom-up: ~1,392 MLD GW / ~2,800 MLD total = ~50%. Either way Bangalore is structurally more groundwater-dependent than Chennai (which is reservoir-impounded) or Madurai (which is Mullaperiyar-fed).
allocation_context._energy_cost_note: Per BWSSB (Wikipedia citation): 75% of agency revenues are consumed by the electricity bill for pumping Cauvery water ~95-100 km uphill against ~500 m elevation gain. This is the single largest factor in Bangalore's water tariff structure and is why every additional MLD via Cauvery is significantly more expensive than equivalent MLD from local sources.

stress_wards_iisc._note: From IISc Groundwater Outlook of Bengaluru City (April 2025), BWSSB-commissioned, names 65 specific wards as 'over-exploited' on the CGWB framework. These 65 are mapped to the pre-Nov 2025 BBMP 198-ward configuration; mapping to GBA 369 wards is a follow-up.
stress_wards_iisc.stress_ward_implication: Per BWSSB's own commissioned study, ~33% of BBMP wards are operating beyond CGWB's 'safe' groundwater extraction limit. Cauvery Stage V was meant to relieve these wards via piped supply; under-delivery means many remain on groundwater + tankers.

tanker_market._note: Bangalore's informal water market is uniquely large among Indian metros. The Ken (May 2026): even at non-crisis times, hundreds of thousands of households substitute tanker water for piped supply.
tanker_market.official_app: Kaveriwheels (BWSSB-operated, ~19K downloads in a 14M city as of 2026, 2.8/5 rating)
tanker_market.informal_rate_note: Crisis-peak summer 2024 rates. Off-season tankers are ~Rs 800-1,200 per 6-12kL but rates surge 2-4x when piped supply fails.
